thread:
customer-it: Hey — after we moved Redwood Private into our VPC, init fails when pulling model artifacts and during runtime calls. Getting TLS errors and 403s. Can you confirm the exact egress destinations we need to allow?

support-jess: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick Qs: are you using a corporate proxy or TLS inspection in your VPC? Any NAT/firewall that does SNI-based ACLs?

customer-it: No explicit proxy. We have an egress allowlist on the firewall (on-prem appliance). No MITM enabled as far as we know. Logs show `TLS handshake failed` and `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` from the app. Also seeing 403 when contacting registry endpoints.

eng-infra-devon: Thanks — two likely causes: 1) you need to allow outbound IPs/hosts for package downloads + Redwood control plane (auth/registry/telemetry) and 2) your firewall may be doing TLS interception, which breaks certificate chain.

eng-ml-sara: To reproduce from your bastion can you run: `curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/v1/health` and `curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/.well-known/openid-configuration` and paste output? That will show whether it's DNS->IP or TLS issue.

customer-it: Ran those. Curl to models.redwood.ai shows: `* SSL: certificate subject name 'redwood.ai' does not match target 'models.redwood.ai'` and `* SSL: certificate signed by unknown authority`. For auth: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`.

eng-infra-devon: The mismatched subject suggests TLS interception or a load balancer swapping certs. The unknown authority error also matches a corporate TLS proxy inserting its own cert. If you have TLS inspection, you must either: a) disable inspection for these hosts, or b) add your inspection CA to the container OS + JVM trust stores.

kamal: Also note we do not support decrypting TLS on our side — our endpoints expect end-to-end TLS with valid CA chains. Some customers whitelist based on SNI (host) + port 443 so the proxy performs passthrough.

eng-ml-sara: For allowlist entries, please ensure your firewall allows outbound TCP 443 to the following hosts (SNI-aware allowlist preferred):
- auth.redwood.ai
- api.redwood.ai
- models.redwood.ai
- registry.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- updates.redwood.ai
- packages.redwood.services
- s3.amazonaws.com (or your configured S3 endpoint for artifact pulls)
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (for pip installs at build time)
- registry.npmjs.org (npm installs)
- registry-1.docker.io, auth.docker.io, and ghcr.io (docker/OCI pulls)

support-jess: If you can't allow hostnames, allow the following IP ranges we use for control plane and artifact hosting: `54.147.0.0/16`, `3.212.0.0/16`, `52.46.0.0/16` (note: these are example ranges — please confirm with our latest account-specific list in the Console under Security -> Network).

oncall-ops: Also check outbound ports: 443 is required for all endpoints; 80 only for redirects during bootstrapping but not for runtime. If you're blocking high ephemeral ports, that can break health checks / callbacks.

customer-it: We do have egress restricted to specific IPs only. Where can I pull the canonical IP list?

eng-infra-devon: In the Console (Customer Settings -> Network) there's a signed JSON of allowed IP blocks and FQDNs. I'll DM you the link and a signed timestamped file. For now, to unblock quickly, add SNI passthrough for `*.redwood.ai` and allow the package hosts above.

customer-it: We tried adding SNI passthrough for `models.redwood.ai` and `auth.redwood.ai`. `curl -v https://auth.redwood.ai/.well-known/openid-configuration` now returns 200, but the app still gets `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` when our JVM tries to call the same endpoint.

eng-infra-devon: JVM containers often use a separate truststore. If TLS inspection is still in the path, you need to import the corporate TLS CA into the JVM cacerts in the container image, or better: exclude these hosts from inspection. Steps to import:
1) obtain the proxy/root CA PEM on your bastion
2) `keytool -import -alias corp-proxy -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts -file corp-proxy.pem` (password default `changeit`)
3) restart the service.

kamal: Another quick debug: run `openssl s_client -showcerts -servername models.redwood.ai -connect models.redwood.ai:443` from the bastion and attach the cert chain. That will confirm if the cert CN/SAN and issuer are our public CA or your proxy.

customer-it: Attached openssl output: issuer CN="Acme Corp TLS Proxy CA" -> looks like interception. We'll escalate to infra team to add corp CA to the image or whitelist.

eng-ml-sara: Good catch. For the 403 you saw earlier against registry endpoints: many customers have an egress ACL that blocks `User-Agent` or missing Host headers for artifact fetcher — but 403 typically means our auth layer couldn't validate the client. Confirm your token exchange (STS) calls to `auth.redwood.ai` are succeeding; we saw your curl to auth is now 200 so tokens should work after TLS fix.

support-jess: I'll open a support ticket and mark as P2 while you sort TLS CA. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min Zoom with infra/eng to walk through bastion tests and the Console IP list.

customer-it: Please do. Also one more ask: Can you provide the minimal allowlist for build-time dependency installs so our CI can run inside the VPC? We only need the minimal set for pip/npm/docker pulls.

eng-infra-devon: Minimal build-time allowlist (SNI hostname allowed outbound over 443):
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- registry.npmjs.org
- registry-1.docker.io & auth.docker.io
- ghcr.io (if using GitHub Packages)
- s3.amazonaws.com (for any model artifact storage)

kamal: Note: if you mirror packages to an internal registry, you'll only need to allow that mirror and outbound to whichever auth provider you use.

support-jess: Ticket #SUP-2026 created and assigned to eng-infra. I posted the Console link in DM. Next actions: customer adds corp CA to JVM or excludes hosts from TLS inspection; temporarily add SNI passthrough for the redwood hosts + package hosts; validate curl/openssl from bastion and paste outputs back here.

customer-it: Thanks — infra team is on it. Will update once they either add CA to image or whitelist hosts. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
